text: Working with APIs is an important skill for modern developers. An API allows two programs to communicate with each other. To get data, you usually send an HTTP request to a specific address, and the server sends back a response, often in JSON format. Many APIs require authentication, which means you need a special key to prove who you are. Be careful with rate limits, because servers only allow a certain number of requests per minute. Finally, always use error handling to deal with problems like a lost connection or an invalid request, so your application stays stable and reliable.
